 Order

Dated this the 10th day of June, 2025 Petitioner is the 3rd accused in Crime No.91 of 2006 registered at the Varandarappilly Police Station, for offences punishable under Sections 408, 420 and 34 of the Indian Penal Code, now pending as C.C.No.1615 of 2024 on the files of the Judicial First Class Magistrate Court, Irinjalakuda.

entities.label: COURT

sentences.text:
2. The crime was registered on the allegation that, during the period from 24.02.1999 to 19.11.1999,
the accused, with the intention to gain unjust profit, misappropriated Rs.4,75,126/- by forging documents of Amballur Service Co-operative Bank, where the 1 st accused was working as the Secretary.

3. Learned Counsel for the petitioner submitted that the dispute, which led to the incident and registration of the crime, is amicably settled and 2025:KER:40897 Annexures A2 and A3 affidavits have been filed by respondents 2 and 3 vouching this fact.
4. Learned Counsel for respondents 2 and 3 also submitted that the dispute is settled and his clients have no grievance against the petitioner.
5. I heard the learned Public Prosecutor also.

6. Having considered the gravity of the offences alleged and having perused the affidavits, the contents of which are vouched to be true and voluntary by the Counsel for respondents 2 and 3, I am satisfied that no public interest is involved in this matter and the dispute has been settled amicably.
In view of the settlement, there is no possibility of the criminal proceedings ending in conviction.

As Indiradevi P V vs State Of Kerala on 10 June, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/176337464/
2 such, continuance of the proceedings will amount to an abuse of process of court and hence, in view of the legal position set out by the Honourable Supreme Court in Madan Mohan 2025:KER:40897 Abbot v State of Punjab [(2008) 4 SCC 582] and Gian Singh v State of Punjab and Another [(2012)
10 SCC 303], there is no impediment in granting the relief.
